# Fairservis 1992, The Harappan Civilization and its Writing, Appendix A; archive.org identifier fairservis-the-harappan-civilization-and-its-writing-1992 (leaves n158-n197; also the-harappan-civilization-and-its-writing)
# language: dra. Read from the page images of the Appendix A tables (Sign No. / Identification / Dravidian Equivalent / DED No. / Homophone / DED No. / Meaning).
# value = Dravidian equivalent as printed (alternatives separated by ' / '; 'hom:' = the homophone column). dedr = Fairservis's DED/DEDR numbers (first = equivalent, after ';' = homophone).
# gloss = his identification of the drawing, then '=>' his meaning. icit = ICIT glyph id matched by drawing against the ICIT render sheets; confidence sure/likely/unsure; unsure rows give candidates as a|b.
# page = printed page number (archive.org leaf in brackets). Fairservis cites seals by Marshall 1931 / Mackay 1937 (MD) numbers, not CISI numbers, so seal confirmation through corpus.tsv was not possible.

kak1988.title: Kak 1988, A frequency analysis of the Indus script (Cryptologia 12(3), 129-143)
kak1988.tsv:
# Kak 1988, A frequency analysis of the Indus script (Cryptologia 12(3), 129-143)
# Table 4 'Tentative identification of the Indus characters', with Brahmi values, p. 136; text p. 137.
# language: sa. Kak draws the signs; only the seven drawings that match one ICIT glyph without doubt are keyed
# (matched against render_glyphs.py sheets). Left out as ambiguous: u (L), o, ga (triangle: 500/480/503),
# ca (bow-tie: 530/550/455), ja (comb pair: 415/416), da, na (inverted T), ba (square), ma, ya (trident: 390/405/407),
# sa's twin sha (plain arrow; the text gives the arrow to ai).
# sign	value	gloss
315	a	H-shaped sign = Brahmi a
520	ai	'arrow with the triangle head' = ai (p. 137)
90	ta	'man' sign = t (p. 137)
700	pa	U = Brahmi pa (p. 137)
900	ra	bracket = Brahmi ra
590	va	box on a stand = Brahmi va
740	sa	jar = sa, the genitive -sya

mahadevan2014.title: Mahadevan 1998 and 2014
mahadevan2014.tsv:
# Mahadevan 1998 and 2014: Dravidian values for the two endings and one four-sign phrase, on ICIT glyph ids.
# language: dra. 'The Arrow Sign in the Indus Script' (harappa.com/arrow, 1998): arrow = *ampu, non-masculine
# singular suffix *-(a)mp(u); jar = masculine singular suffix *-(a)nru. 'Dravidian Proof of the Indus Script via
# the Rig Veda' (Bulletin of the IRC 4, 2014): WOLF HOOK CROSSROADS JAR = mar-kol-pat-(a)nr- 'merchant of the city',
# his Fig. 2 = CISI II M-857, ICIT 255 435 690 740.
# sign	value	gloss
740	anru	jar; masculine singular suffix -(a)nru, 'he of the'
520	ampu	arrow; non-masculine singular suffix -(a)mpu
255	mar	wolf; barter, barterer
435	kol	hook; receiving, receiver
690	pat	crossroads; settlement, resident
